Set T(z,h)=(sqrt(1−d(z)²h²)X(z),d(z)h). E,T have identical full first jet at h=0; hence Psi=E inverse composed T=id+O(h²), DPsi=I+O(h) uniformly on a fixed compact planar box. First shrink actual heights by a positive constant. Cut off Psi−id in a larger z-box and thin height slab eta; cutoff derivative O(1/eta) multiplies O(eta²), so the total perturbation derivative is O(eta). The interpolation id+t cutoff(Psi−id) has derivative difference norm<1/2 for sufficiently small eta, is injective by the global Lipschitz bound, proper and onto, and gives an orientation-preserving compactly supported ambient isotopy. In collar coordinates the same planar base z and positive height d(z)h preserve all crossing orders.
